Multi-Stage Production Cost Modeling

Now, we are ready to put pieces together. We will define, solve, analyze, and visualize a multi-stage production cost model over the course of a year with two decision stages: a day ahead, hourly resolution unit commitment, followed by an hourly resolution economic dispatch.

  1. Set up a default unit commitment model
template = template_unit_commitment()
Network Model
Network Model PowerSimulations.CopperPlatePowerModel
Slacks false
PTDF false
Duals None
Device Models
Device Type Formulation Slacks
PowerSystems.ThermalStandard PowerSimulations.ThermalBasicUnitCommitment false
PowerSystems.RenewableDispatch PowerSimulations.RenewableFullDispatch false
PowerSystems.PowerLoad PowerSimulations.StaticPowerLoad false
PowerSystems.RenewableNonDispatch PowerSimulations.FixedOutput false
PowerSystems.InterruptiblePowerLoad PowerSimulations.PowerLoadInterruption false
Branch Models
Branch Type Formulation Slacks
PowerSystems.Transformer2W PowerSimulations.StaticBranch false
PowerSystems.Line PowerSimulations.StaticBranch false
PowerSystems.TwoTerminalHVDCLine PowerSimulations.HVDCTwoTerminalDispatch false
PowerSystems.TapTransformer PowerSimulations.StaticBranch false
Service Models
Service Type Formulation Slacks Aggregated Model
PowerSystems.VariableReserve{PowerSystems.ReserveUp} PowerSimulations.RangeReserve false true
PowerSystems.VariableReserve{PowerSystems.ReserveDown} PowerSimulations.RangeReserve false true 
solver = optimizer_with_attributes(HiGHS.Optimizer, "mip_rel_gap" => 0.5)
MathOptInterface.OptimizerWithAttributes(HiGHS.Optimizer, Pair{MathOptInterface.AbstractOptimizerAttribute, Any}[MathOptInterface.RawOptimizerAttribute("mip_rel_gap") => 0.5])
  1. Apply that template to our data to make a complete model, with both data and equations:
models = SimulationModels(;
    decision_models = [
        DecisionModel(template, system; optimizer = solver, name = "UC"),
    ],
)
Decision Models
Model Name Model Type Status Output Directory
UC GenericOpProblem EMPTY nothing
No Emulator Model Specified

We just have one model – the unit commitment model.

  1. In addition to defining the formulation template, sequential simulations require definitions for how information flows between problems to set the initial conditions of the next problem:
DA_sequence = SimulationSequence(;
    models = models,
    ini_cond_chronology = InterProblemChronology(),
)
Simulation Sequence
Simulation Step Interval 24 hours
Number of Problems 1
Simulation Problems
Model Name Horizon Interval Executions Per Step
UC 2 days 1 day 1
  1. Finally, put together the models and the flow of information between them to simulate 3 days of a unit commitment:
sim = Simulation(;
    name = "default_UC",
    steps = 3,
    models = models,
    sequence = DA_sequence,
    simulation_folder = mktempdir(; cleanup = true),
)
Simulation
Simulation Name default_UC
Build Status EMPTY
Run Status NOT_READY

UC 2 days 1 day 1
  1. Build the simulation, which does all the equation preparation before executing:
build!(sim; recorders = [:simulation])
InfrastructureSystems.Simulation.SimulationBuildStatusModule.SimulationBuildStatus.BUILT = 0
  1. Simulate!
execute!(sim)
InfrastructureSystems.Simulation.RunStatusModule.RunStatus.SUCCESSFULLY_FINALIZED = 0
  1. Now, load in the simulation results from the output files:
results = SimulationResults(sim)
uc_results = get_decision_problem_results(results, "UC")

  1. Let's visualize the results

<!– @example pcm4 # plot_fuel(uc_results);–>

  1. We can also look at how much it cost to operate the thermal generators at each time step:
costs =
    read_realized_expressions(uc_results, list_expression_names(uc_results))["ProductionCostExpression__ThermalStandard"]

Wind, solar, and hydro have 0 operating cost and do not contribute to total cost in this model

  1. We can sum over the set of generators and time-steps to get total production cost for this window
sum(sum(eachcol(costs[!, 2:end])))
8.025416529200557e6

Now, let's change some things in the system:

  1. Now, let's change how the thermal generators behave by adding in ramping and minimum up and down time constraints:
set_device_model!(template, ThermalStandard, ThermalStandardUnitCommitment)
┌ Warning: Overwriting PowerSystems.ThermalStandard existing model
└ @ PowerSimulations ~/.julia/packages/PowerSimulations/89s3Q/src/core/device_model.jl:116

You can see the formulations options in the documentation: https://nrel-sienna.github.io/PowerSimulations.jl/stable/formulation_library/ThermalGen/

  1. We've changed our template, so we need to re-build the DecisionModels within our simulation, which includes a copy of the template:
models = SimulationModels(;
    decision_models = [
        DecisionModel(template, system; optimizer = solver, name = "UC"),
    ],
)
DA_sequence = SimulationSequence(;
    models = models,
    ini_cond_chronology = InterProblemChronology(),
)
sim = Simulation(;
    name = "default_UC",
    steps = 3,
    models = models,
    sequence = DA_sequence,
    simulation_folder = mktempdir(; cleanup = true),
)

build!(sim; recorders = [:simulation]);
execute!(sim)

uc_results = get_decision_problem_results(results, "UC")

Adding in renewables

  1. Now, let's add in those large-scale wind and solar plants by making them available again:
for g in get_components(RenewableDispatch, system)
    set_available!(g, true)
end
  1. We've changed the data, not the template formulations, so this time we just need to re-build and simulate:
build!(sim; recorders = [:simulation]);
execute!(sim)
InfrastructureSystems.Simulation.RunStatusModule.RunStatus.SUCCESSFULLY_FINALIZED = 0
  1. Let's re-extract the results and take a look at the impact on the dispatch stack:
results = SimulationResults(sim)
uc_results = get_decision_problem_results(results, "UC")
# plot_fuel(uc_results);
